title: Shipping giants reroute vessels as Houthi attacks in Red Sea raise supply chain fears
text: Major container lines warned on Monday that attacks on ships in the Red Sea could disrupt global supply chains for weeks. Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd said they were pausing transits through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, a chokepoint for Asia-Europe trade. The companies said rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope would add 10 days to voyages and raise freight costs. Analysts said the disruptions may delay electronics and automotive parts deliveries into European factories ahead of the holiday season.

title: Maersk says Red Sea disruption now expected to last months
text: Maersk confirmed on Sunday that container traffic through the Suez Canal has been halted since late November and now expects the disruption to last several months, delaying deliveries of semiconductors and auto parts to European manufacturers.

title: City council approves new park funding
text: The city council approved $2 million in funding for a new riverside park on Tuesday. Construction is expected to begin in the spring.
